mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly uses the universal quantifier to express that every integer n satisfies n² ≥ n?

options.A: For all integers n, n² ≥ n.
options.B: There exists an integer n such that n² ≥ n.
options.C: If n is an integer, then n² < n.
options.D: For some integer n, n² = n.

mcqs.answer: For all integers n, n² ≥ n.
mcqs.explanation: The universal quantifier (∀) states that a property holds for every element of the domain. Option A reads “For all integers n, n² ≥ n,” which is exactly the universal form. Option B uses an existential quantifier, C gives a false implication, and D refers to a particular element, not all.

mcqs.question: In a class of 30 students, at least one student scored above 90% in the test. Which statement correctly uses the existential quantifier to represent this situation?

options.A: For every student, the score is above 90%.
options.B: There exists a student in the class who scored above 90%.

mcqs.answer: There exists a student in the class who scored above 90%.
mcqs.explanation: The existential quantifier (∃) asserts that at least one element satisfies the property. Option B states exactly that – there is at least one student with a score above 90%. Options A and D describe universal statements, while C is the negation of the given fact.

mcqs.question: Identify the incorrectly translated quantified statement:

options.A: ∀x (x is a prime number → x > 1) translates to “Every prime number is greater than 1.”
options.B: ∃x (x is even ∧ x < 2) translates to “There exists an even number less than 2.”
options.C: ∀x (x > 0) translates to “There exists a number greater than 0.”
options.D: ∃x (x² = 4) translates to “There exists a number whose square is 4.”

mcqs.answer: ∀x (x > 0) translates to “There exists a number greater than 0.”
mcqs.explanation: Option C misinterprets the universal quantifier. ∀x (x > 0) means “Every number is greater than 0,” not “There exists a number…”. The other options correctly match their quantifiers and translations.

mcqs.question: What is the correct negation of the statement “∀x (P(x) → Q(x))”?
mcqs.explanation: Negating a universal conditional gives an existential statement where the antecedent holds but the consequent fails: ¬∀x (P → Q) ≡ ∃x (P ∧ ¬Q). Options B, C, and D do not represent the proper logical negation.

mcqs.question: Which pair correctly contrasts the truth conditions of universal (∀) and existential (∃) quantifiers?

options.A: ∀x P(x) is true only if P(x) holds for at least one element; ∃x P(x) is true only if P(x) holds for all elements.
options.B: ∀x P(x) is true only if P(x) holds for every element; ∃x P(x) is true if P(x) holds for at least one element.
options.C: Both ∀x P(x) and ∃x P(x) require P(x) to hold for all elements.
options.D: Both ∀x P(x) and ∃x P(x) require P(x) to hold for at least one element.

mcqs.answer: ∀x P(x) is true only if P(x) holds for every element; ∃x P(x) is true if P(x) holds for at least one element.
mcqs.explanation: The universal quantifier demands the predicate be true for every member of the domain, while the existential quantifier needs the predicate to be true for at least one member. Option B states this precisely; the other options invert or conflate the conditions.

mcqs.question: In the set S = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, which statement is equivalent to “∃x∈S such that x is a prime number and x > 2”?

options.A: 2 is the only prime number in S.
options.B: There exists a prime number in S that is greater than 2.
options.C: All prime numbers in S are greater than 2.
options.D: No prime numbers in S are greater than 2.

mcqs.answer: There exists a prime number in S that is greater than 2.
mcqs.explanation: The original existential statement asserts the existence of at least one element of S that is both prime and greater than 2. Option B restates this directly. Option A mentions only 2 (which is not >2), C makes a universal claim, and D contradicts the existence claim.

mcqs.question: Select the statement that correctly translates the quantified expression ∀x (x is a natural number → x ≥ 0).

options.A: Every natural number is greater than or equal to zero.
options.B: There exists a natural number that is greater than zero.

mcqs.answer: Every natural number is greater than or equal to zero.
mcqs.explanation: The universal quantifier (∀) together with the implication translates to “For every x, if x is a natural number then x ≥ 0,” which is exactly option A. Options B, C, and D either change the quantifier or state false properties.

mcqs.question: What is the negation of the existential statement “∃x (x is a rational number and x² = 2)”?

options.A: For every x, either x is not rational or x² ≠ 2.
options.B: There exists an x that is rational and x² = 2.
options.C: There exists an x that is irrational and x² = 2.
options.D: For some x, x is rational and x² ≠ 2.

mcqs.answer: For every x, either x is not rational or x² ≠ 2.
mcqs.explanation: Negating an existential quantifier yields a universal statement with the negated predicate: ¬∃x (R(x) ∧ Q(x)) ≡ ∀x (¬R(x) ∨ ¬Q(x)). Option A expresses this correctly. Options B and C repeat or modify the original claim, while D is only a partial negation.
